intro.heading: One place to know what to do when you're new here.
intro.text: The Portal brings the onboarding roadmap, approved documents and contacts into one place: tasks in the right order, sourced answers, and Viga saying so honestly when there is no basis instead of guessing.

chat.label: Ask Viga, with sources
chat.sub: You ask, Viga answers from the documents
chat.titleEnd: in force on the day you ask.
chat.body: Ask about house rules, leave, benefits or security. Viga only uses approved documents that are in force and answers with verbatim quotes so you can check for yourself. With no basis, Viga says so.

process.label: Onboarding roadmap
process.body: Each task in the roadmap has clear guidance, with contacts and related documents; mark it "Done" yourself when finished, and dependent tasks unlock automatically. No heavy approval process. This feature is being built alongside the VSF Onboarding Portal.

ticket.label: Viga and tickets
ticket.titleEnd: , open a ticket if you need help.
ticket.body: When you're stuck on a task in the roadmap, ask Viga right there in context. If Viga has no basis, it says so and offers to open a ticket to HR — only after you confirm. This feature is being built.

chat.title: VSF Onboarding Assistant
chat.label: SOURCED Q&A
chat.question: How many days of annual leave do permanent employees get?
chat.answer: Permanent employees get 12 days of annual leave, according to the 2024 annual leave policy.
chat.placeholder: Ask about house rules, leave, devices, accounts...

s1.label: Submit a request with form IT-SW-01 on the IT portal

s2.label: IT forwards it to VinSOC, which scans within 3 working days

s3.label: Only download from the approved software catalogue

s4.label: Never open install links received by chat or email

asker.title: New employee

viga.infoLink: What can Viga do, and not do?
viga.infoIntro: Viga works from your own onboarding journey and the documents HR published in the portal. Viga only guides you: it never decides for you and never changes a task's status.
